title: The 5 Longest Animal Migrations, Ranked (#1 Is Not a Whale)
subject: migrating animal

scenes.text: You'd expect a whale to win this one. It doesn't even come close.

scenes.label: Humpback whale · 10,000 mi
scenes.text: Number five: the humpback whale. Roughly ten thousand miles a year between cold feeding waters and warm breeding ones.

scenes.label: Elephant seal · 13,000 mi
scenes.text: Number four: the northern elephant seal. Up to thirteen thousand miles a year, and almost all of it spent at sea.

scenes.label: Gray whale · 14,000 mi
scenes.text: Number three: the gray whale. One tagged female swam about fourteen thousand miles there and back, in just 172 days.

scenes.label: Sooty shearwater · 40,000 mi
scenes.text: Number two: the sooty shearwater. This seabird loops around the whole Pacific, about forty thousand miles a year.

scenes.label: Arctic tern · 44,000 mi
scenes.text: Number one: the Arctic tern. About forty-four thousand miles a year, pole to pole and back. A bird beats every whale.

description:
The five longest animal migrations, ranked by distance travelled in a year.
The winner isn't a whale. The Arctic tern flies roughly 44,000 miles every year, from the Arctic to Antarctica and back, with the sooty shearwater close behind at around 40,000 miles.
Which one surprised you most?
first_comment: Which animal would you have put at number one, and what should we rank next?
